root_idea.summary: The root centers on rectifying or bringing something into proper order, with related ideas of skilled apprehension, quick understanding, and gaining hold of what is perceived.
root_idea.development: The semantic development moves from straightening a crooked object to being skilled in understanding or acquiring something, then to perceiving, finding, seizing, and gaining mastery over what is reached.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The group is represented under the normalized Form I perfect citation form ثَقِفَ, which covers its active and passive Quranic inflections.

senses.definition: To perceive, detect, find, or encounter someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage this includes finding or encountering by observation or attainment; the usage may be active or passive and is not restricted to a particular object class.

senses.definition: To catch, overtake, seize, overcome, or gain mastery over someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Especially attested in contexts of war or confrontation. The construction can describe one party gaining possession or mastery over another, including passive forms meaning to be found, caught, or overcome.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become skilled, intelligent, quick, sharp, or sagacious; to acquire or understand something quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical use describing personal ability or rapid mastery of knowledge, speech, an art, or a craft.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of vinegar: to be or become very acid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This reported usage is attached specifically to vinegar and is presented tentatively in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To thrust or pierce someone with a spear or similar weapon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive physical action directed at a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To straighten, even, or correct something crooked, especially a spear, bow, or similar object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action is performed with a ثِقَاف, a tool used for straightening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To discipline, educate, amend, or improve a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of physically straightening or correcting something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make food acid or sour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of vinegar's effect on food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie with or strive to surpass another in skill, intelligence, or successful attainment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived reciprocal form can also describe contending with another in combat or with swords or other weapons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be made or appointed to gain mastery over or overcome someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive construction describing an encounter or assignment in which mastery is gained.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become disciplined, well educated, amended, or improved.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or medio-passive development of the Form II sense of disciplining and improving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend or play with one another using swords or other weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal combat usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Skilled, intelligent, sharp, or quick to understand and learn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a person who quickly understands what is said, catches what is thrown, or is adept in an art or craft; it may also describe someone quick to seize an opponent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Contention or combat, especially fighting with a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use comparable to ثِقَافٌ in describing armed contest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Skill, intelligence, or sagacity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal expression of skilled apprehension or ability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An instrument for straightening spears, bows, and other crooked objects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Typically an iron implement or strong piece of wood used to press and correct the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The handle of a shield of the type called حَجَفَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical or equipment term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Very acid or sour, especially of vinegar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive adjective applied to vinegar; the same entry also records other derived uses separately.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing in which one is skilled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal or adjectival use referring to an object of acquired expertise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who has been thrust or pierced with a spear or similar weapon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived descriptive use for the person affected by the action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The use or handling of a sword, especially skillful performance with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal term for proficiency or performance in sword use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most skilled, especially in contending or playing with swords or other weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spear that has been straightened or made even.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may poetically be extended to the spear itself.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I skill and sagacity meaning.
Being skilled in a thing is covered by the Form I skill meaning.
Contains Quran-attested perception, finding, seizure, mastery, and rapid understanding branches.
Reciprocal striving to surpass in skill or attainment.
Armed contention is included as a combat specialization of reciprocal competition.
Passive appointment or being made to overcome.
Adjectival skill, intelligence, and quick understanding.
Quick seizure of opponents is included in the adjective's stated range.
Thing in which one is skilled.
Descriptive use for a pierced man.

cautions: The reported vinegar sense under ثَقُفَ is explicitly accompanied by a manuscript-error suspicion in the lexical evidence; it is retained as a tentative Classical usage rather than treated as Quranic evidence.

The Quranic form group contains active and passive Form I inflections; the public headword is normalized to the classical citation form ثَقِفَ rather than copied from the internal QAC lemma candidate.
